claims.claim: Q2 2026 revenue reached a record $234M, up 62% year over year, and backlog reached a record $2.36B, up 137% year over year.
Rocket Lab reported more than $437M of new launch contracts across Electron, HASTE and Neutron during Q2 plus post-quarter signings, with 90+ launches in total launch backlog.

At Sep. 17, 2026 market capitalization was about $40.59B against TTM revenue of about $769M; P/S was about 52.85 and shares outstanding were up 15.68% year over year, making valuation and dilution material risks despite rapid growth.

thesisQuality.basis: Record revenue/backlog and expanding launch plus space-systems scope support a strong integrated-space thesis, tempered by execution intensity.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Q2 revenue rose 62% YoY to a record $234M and backlog rose 137% YoY to $2.36B.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: About $40.59B market cap and ~52.85x sales against a still loss-making business embed substantial expectations.

catalystScore.basis: 90+ launch backlog, Neutron development, and more than $1B of new Q3 contracts cited by management create multiple execution catalysts.

governancePower.basis: Founder-led execution has expanded contracts and vertical scope, while aggressive acquisition/capital strategy warrants a governance discount.

alignment2036.basis: Launch, spacecraft, communications and defense infrastructure directly align with expanding orbital infrastructure needs.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Launch services, space systems and planned communications ownership create explicit vertical integration across the stack.

bottleneckControl.basis: Integrated launch plus spacecraft capability controls multiple scarce execution steps, though larger launch and satellite competitors remain.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Commercial, civil and national-security demand diversify end markets, but Neutron and acquisition execution create scenario sensitivity.

substitutionResilience.basis: Flight heritage, backlog and vertical integration increase switching friction, but launch and spacecraft alternatives remain credible.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Vertical integration improves control of critical subsystems, while aerospace supply chains and development programs remain capital- and component-intensive.

pricingPower.basis: Rapid backlog growth and contract wins support value capture, but current evidence does not establish monopoly pricing power.

riskEvidence.basis: Primary risks are extreme valuation, continuing losses, 15.68% YoY share-count growth, Neutron execution and integration/capital requirements.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Current issuer operating evidence and independent current market data support all numeric components; customer-level backlog concentration remains a non-gating unknown.
